text:
maria (Customer): Hey team — after our corp proxy/WPAD rollout our on-prem service calls to Redwood are failing. We see either 407 Proxy Authentication Required or SSL handshake errors. Can you help?

emma (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste one of the curl -v outputs from a failing host?

maria (Customer): Sure, two short snippets:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com
> CONNECT api.redwood.example.com:443 HTTP/1.1\n< HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required
```
and on another host: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com
* SSL: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```

liam (Eng): Sounds like either the proxy is requiring auth (407) or doing TLS inspection and presenting a corp cert. Did you enable WPAD/PAC today?

maria (Customer): Yes, we pushed WPAD via DHCP option 252 earlier this morning. We think non-browser clients are auto-picking it up. How do we prove that?

noah (SRE): A couple quick checks: 
- Fetch the PAC: `curl -v http://wpad/wpad.dat` or `curl -v http://<wpad-host>/wpad.dat`
- DNS check: `dig +short wpad`
- Check env: `env | egrep -i "proxy|no_proxy"`
- Inspect TLS chain: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com`
If openssl shows a subject like `CN=corp-proxy-inspect` and an issuer of your corp CA, it's MITM.

maria (Customer): Ran openssl — cert subject is `CN=corp-proxy-inspect.local` and issuer is our corp root CA. So it's TLS inspection and our runtime doesn't trust that CA -> SSL errors.

emma (Support): Two remediation paths: 1) Preferred: have network/proxy do CONNECT passthrough for Redwood endpoints (SNI passthrough) or add an egress rule to bypass MITM for those FQDNs/IPs. 2) If passthrough isn't possible, add your corp root CA to the OS/container truststore or JVM cacerts used by your service (not ideal for security).

liam (Eng): Quick troubleshooting tip: try ignoring proxy to confirm: `curl -v --noproxy "*" https://api.redwood.example.com` — if that works, WPAD/proxy is the culprit. Also test explicit proxy to see auth flow: `curl -v -x http://proxy.company.local:3128 https://api.redwood.example.com` to reproduce 407.

maria (Customer): `--noproxy` succeeded. Netops will need an allowlist. What exact hosts/IPs to give them?

noah (SRE): Ask them to allow outbound TCP/443 to `api.redwood.example.com` (and any hostnames listed in your Private/VPC onboarding doc). For hosted customers we publish egress IP ranges in the onboarding portal — provide those to netops. Request SNI passthrough or TLS passthrough for those destinations so the proxy doesn't MITM. If they cannot, instruct how to install the corp root CA into your container images/service runtimes.

emma (Support): Note: our SDK also validates cert chains and performs pinning by default for Private deployments. If your proxy rewrites certs, you either need a passthrough or to update the runtime trust bundle. We can help with the exact truststore commands if you tell us the runtime (docker, debian, jvm, python).

maria (Customer): We'll open a ticket with netops to request bypass for `api.redwood.example.com` and to look at WPAD. One more question — is there any temporary workaround to avoid code changes?

liam (Eng): Temporary hacky options: run a small sidecar in your network that terminates TLS to Redwood and forwards over the corp proxy (with the corp CA trusted on the sidecar), or build an explicit egress route/NAT that skips the proxy. Both are operational workarounds — long term, TLS passthrough is cleaner.

ops-bot: Ticket SUP-4872 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to liam (Eng) and ops.

maria (Customer): Thanks all — opening netops request now. Will update here once they confirm :thumbsup:
